item.title: [ 50] Beat E33 today, have opinions, you fags ready? Expedition 33 is more than ju
item.description:
Beat E33 today, have opinions, you fags ready?

Expedition 33 is more than just an outstanding game, it's a celebration of the values that hold a society together: ethincity. From beginning to end, the story radiates a deep sense of national pride, portraying ordinary people who refuse to surrender their heritage, culture, and identity in the face of overwhelming odds. The characters aren't driven by selfish ambition but by a commitment to something larger than themselves: their homeland, their community, and future generations.

What impressed me most was the emphasis on family. Whether through blood relations or the bonds forged through shared sacrifice, Expedition 33 constantly reminds players that strength comes from standing together. The emotional core of the narrative is built on loyalty, duty, and the willingness to protect loved ones even when the cost is immense. These themes never feel forced; they're woven naturally into the journey and give every victory and loss greater meaning.

The game's world feels rich with history and tradition, creating a powerful sense of belonging. Rather than glorifying individual heroics alone, it highlights collective courage and the importance of preserving the values that define a people. In an era when many stories focus on cynicism and division, Expedition 33 offers something refreshing: a heartfelt tribute to unity, resilience, and the enduring importance of family.

Combined with its stunning visuals, memorable characters, and compelling gameplay, E33 stands as a remarkable achievement. It's the kind of experience that leaves players not only entertained but inspired, reminding us that our greatest strength comes from the people and traditions we cherish most.

I wish /v/ was white enough for this game.

item.title: [ 33] /tcg/ Trading Card Game General
item.description:
Championed Edition

>I want to learn the game, where do I begin?
Download PTCGL at https://tcg.pokemon.com/en-us/tcgl
The game has a quick tutorial and a bunch of decent decks to get you started against other beginners or against the AI. Some of those decks are very close to meta too. You can also go to your local game store and see if people are playing Pokémon.

>I know how to play, how do I make my own deck?
You have a decent beginner's guide at https://www.justinbasil.com/guide
There's also the old /tcg/ guide at https://imgur.com/a/W4NkOu6
After that, look up meta decks and try to reverse engineer them to see how things work.

>Where to find meta decks?
For big irl events, go to https://limitlesstcg.com/decks
For online events, go to https://play.limitlesstcg.com/decks?game=PTCG
For japanese events, go to https://pokecabook.com/archives/1417

item.title: [ 33] Energy Department says advanced nuclear reactor first to reach critical milestone
item.description:
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/energy-department-says-advanced-nuclear-reactor-first-to-reach-critical-milestone

WASHINGTON (AP) — The Energy Department says a small nuclear reactor under development at a national lab has reached a crucial milestone that could allow it to produce electricity within a few years.

The microreactor being developed by Antares Nuclear Inc. at the Idaho National Lab reached "criticality" on Thursday, Energy Secretary Chris Wright said. The milestone occurs when a nuclear reactor achieves a self-sustaining chain reaction capable of producing a steady release of energy.

Antares is the first private company to bring an advanced reactor to criticality under a pilot program begun last year by the Trump administration meant to supercharge nuclear energy production in the U.S. The demonstration was conducted in partnership with the Energy Department and other contractors with support from the U.S. Army.

"We are very excited by this news today," Wright said Friday on a call with reporters. "I think June 4th will be a historic day in the American nuclear renaissance."

item.title: [ 89] /out/ings with a pipe
item.description:
Last thread >>2856593

This is a thread for enjoying a pipe while doing outdoor activities. If you ask why this belongs on /out/, you've never spent
an evening by the campfire with a pipe silently enjoying the nature around you, and you're missing out.

>how to get started
Purchase a corn cob pipe (or a cheap briar pipe) and a pouch of Half and Half or Captain Black tobacco from a smoke shop
or online. You will need a lighter or match, and something to tamp it with--a large nail works well if you don't have a pipe tool.
Fill the pipe with tobacco, pack it down halfway, top it off, pack it down to 3/4, top it off again, pack gently and enjoy. Smoke
slower than you think you need to, the tobacco tastes best when it is burning cool. Tamp and re-light as needed. If you still
have trouble, try different methods on YouTube until you find one that works for you.
>smoking a pipe will give you cancer
Originally the Surgeon General found that pipe and cigar smokers, following a careful study of the statistics (at a time when
most adults smoked, so they had a good sample size), had insignificant death rate increases. Nowadays, tobacco is being
legislated against while hard drugs are being legalized. Put two and two together. Tobacco is just another good thing under attack by the government.

>muh weed
Not the time or place. Start your own thread.

All tobacco users welcome.
